Note: Corpus PR StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#280 asks what a filter naming SEVERAL ranges selects. Real BC answers the UNION of them: measured on a 28.4.53241.0 service tier, '1..50|200000..' yields 1,2,...,50,200000,200001,... and its mirror '..-200000|1..50' yields 50,...,1,-200000,-200001,.... The runner serves this table from a materialised in-memory store, so an alternative that is open at one end cannot be followed: BC substitutes its own +-1000000000 for the open end, which makes this filter 999,800,051 rows. The runner REFUSES it loudly instead - RunnerOutOfScopeException, 'out-of-scope: Integer (virtual table 2000000026) - not-yet-implemented - integer-virtual-table: an Integer filter names Number 200000 with its other end open, outside the base window [-1000..100000] an open bound is answered from' - rather than materialising ~1e9 rows or, as it did before #3471, quietly serving the request from the base window with the 50 rows of the first range and dropping the second whole. The refusal is decided per range since #3471, which is what this test pins on the runner side; the same PR's tests/runner-extras/integer-virtual-table-window arms (codeunit 64591) pin the refusal itself. MODE: expect-oos, because a refusal IS an out-of-scope signal and the two other modes do not fit - expect-divergence means 'answers differently and does not signal', and expect-fail-known-gap requires an issue that stays open after the PR merges, which #3471 does not (it closes with the fix). ANCHOR: the throw emits 'not-yet-implemented - integer-virtual-table: ...' and ExpectationManifest.ReasonAnchor cuts at the first em-dash, so 'not-yet-implemented' is the anchor this entry carries. That anchor also buys the tear-through past an AL [TryFunction] (ApplicationObjectBasePatches.IsPermanentOutOfScope), which is right here: a service tier DOES answer this read, so trapping it into false would restore the silent default. WHAT WOULD REMOVE THIS ENTRY: #3485, which tracks answering an open-ended Integer range the way BC does rather than from the base window or with a refusal; it stays open after #3471 merges. The other two arms of codeunit 60368 added by corpus #280 are NOT declared here and must pass: Record_Integer_TwoClosedRanges_CountTheirUnion (two closed ranges, 60 rows, materialised under the row cap) and Record_Integer_KeyedGetPastOneBillion_AnswersFalse (the +-1e9 clamp, which the runner already matches).
